schedule.label: Theme by date
schedule.help: Wear another theme between two days (for example the festive theme for Eid). Outside these days the shop wears the theme above.

previewParam.label: Try a theme with a link
previewParam.help: When on, adding ?theme=noir (or classic, ivory, festive) to a shop address shows that theme to you only. Customers keep seeing the real one.

colours.label: Your own colours
colours.help: Change single colours of the theme. A colour that makes text hard to read is refused and the theme's own colours stay.

fonts.label: Fonts
fonts.help: The letters for body text and for headings. Only fonts the shop carries itself can be chosen, so pages stay fast.

logoPhone.label: Logo for phones
logoPhone.help: A smaller or simpler logo for the phone header. Empty: the main logo is used.

favicon.label: Small icon in the browser tab
favicon.help: A square picture, at least 512 by 512 pixels.

sloganShort.label: Short slogan
sloganShort.help: Shown under the name on small phones when the full slogan does not fit. In English and Bengali.

logoSize.label: Logo size
logoSize.help: How tall the logo is drawn in the desktop header, the phone header and the footer, in pixels.

logoStyle.label: Logo style
logoStyle.help: How the shop's name is drawn in the desktop header and the desktop footer: 0 keeps it as it was, 1 to 10 are the other styles. The phone keeps its logo. An uploaded logo picture always wins.

hours.label: Opening hours
hours.help: When customers can reach you, for example Sat–Thu 10am–8pm. Shown beside WhatsApp and the hotline. In English and Bengali.

announce.label: Announcement bar
announce.help: The thin line at the very top. Each message can have a start and end day. A message that promises free delivery or Cash on Delivery only shows once those are switched on.

header.label: Header icons
header.help: Which buttons sit in the header and in what order, and whether the slogan shows under the name.

menu.label: Menus and bottom bar
menu.help: The links in the phone menu, the help links under them and the 3 to 5 buttons of the phone's bottom bar. Categories join on their own.

desktopNav.label: Desktop menu row
desktopNav.help: How the desktop menu row is arranged (main categories + More, every category, one Shop menu, or roomy with the rest under More), how many categories stay in the row, whether the menu opens as a small list or a wide panel, and which links it shows. Phones are not affected.

footer.label: Footer
footer.help: The desktop footer's design (the reference layout or the earlier one), the promise line, the columns of links with their shorter desktop words and an optional small icon beside each, the contact buttons, social links and payment marks. A promise or mark for Cash on Delivery only shows once it is switched on.

enabled.label: Bengali shop
enabled.help: The shop in Bengali under /bn, with the language switch in the header and menu.

readyPages.label: Bengali pages that are ready
readyPages.help: Bengali pages are hidden from Google until they are marked ready here, so a half-translated page is never found.

digits.label: Bengali digits
digits.help: On the Bengali shop, numbers and prices are written in Bengali digits (১২৩).

labels.label: Your own words
labels.help: Change any word or sentence of the shop, in English and Bengali. Empty: the shop's own words are used.

engine.label: How rows slide
engine.help: Rows of products move slowly on their own. They stop under the mouse, while a finger holds them and while the keyboard is in them, and start again afterwards.

sections.label: Home page sections
sections.help: Which parts the home page shows and in what order: the hero, categories, new in, sets, size finder, flash sale, shop the look, reviews and the journal. A part with nothing to show yet stays hidden on its own.

hero.label: Home hero
hero.help: The big panel at the top: the small line, the title, the line under it, up to three buttons and the promise lines. A promise line only shows when its rule is on (Cash on Delivery, size exchange). On a desktop the coloured panel can reach further right (0 to 240 px). Each text can be your own words in English and Bengali; the default words name no count, season or year, so write a campaign's own (a season, how many new styles) only while it is true.

heroSlides.label: Hero pictures
heroSlides.help: The pictures sliding beside the hero text: how many (12 to 15 reads well), the most from one category so every category gets a turn, or a collection that fills them instead while its dates run (a campaign). Only products in stock, if you like. How fast they glide, how long one arrow tap takes, and on a desktop how wide they fade into the text (80 or 140 px) with an optional soft wash. Phones can show the arrows too (off = the approved phone look). A picture is the product's photo of that colour, or its drawing until the photo is uploaded.

categories.label: Category tiles
categories.help: The "Shop by category" tiles: the most tiles shown and where "Shop all" goes. Each tile shows the first product of the category and how many styles it has.

newIn.label: New in
newIn.help: How many products the "New in" row shows, newest first or in your own order, and where "View all" goes.

reviews.label: Customer reviews row
reviews.help: How many approved reviews slide on the home page (up to 10), the fewest stars a review needs, and whether the average shows beside the heading. With no approved review the row stays hidden.

rowFade.label: Soft edges on sliding rows
rowFade.help: Sliding rows fade out at both edges. Off = plain straight edges.

page.label: Category page layout
page.help: The breadcrumb (Home / category) above the title, how many products one page shows before "Show more" (4 to 120), where sold-out styles go (kept in your order, moved to the end, or left out), from how few styles a desktop page drops the filter column (0 = never), and the "Showing 12 of 30" line with its bar.

filters.label: Category filters
filters.help: Which filter groups show and in what order: in stock only, size, colour, fit and price. Every option is built from the category's own products, with live counts; an option no product matches is dimmed (sizes crossed out) or left out. How many colours show before "+ more colours", the line under the sizes, the rounding steps of the price bands (in poisha) and, per category, two hand-set price cut points or none.

toolbar.label: Phone filter row and quick chips
toolbar.help: The phone's top row (Filter, Sort, On sale: switch each on or off, rename it, change the order) and the quick chips under it: tick the chips you want from the library, in your order. A chip that would match every product or none in a category is left out by itself. "My size only" and "Set price" join when Find My Size and the sets can tell which products qualify. Each category can switch its own row and chips off or tick its own chips.

sort.label: Sort choices
sort.help: Which sorts the customer can pick and in what order (recommended = your own order, newest, price low to high, price high to low, top rated). The first one is how the page opens. Each can carry your own words.

newIn.label: "New in" page
newIn.help: The New in page lists the newest published styles of every shown category: by publish date or your own order, and only from the last so many days (0 = every style).

faq.label: Category questions
faq.help: The shop-wide questions under each category's own: switch each on or off, change its words, change the order. A question that promises something (Cash on Delivery, free delivery, exchange) shows only while that rule is on. Whether the first question starts open.

seo.label: Category text for Google
seo.help: Per category, your own: the title in the browser tab and Google, the line under it in Google, the heading of the text block and the text itself (a blank line starts a new paragraph). A category with no text shows no text block.

faqOwn.label: Each category's own questions
faqOwn.help: Per category, your own questions and answers about its clothes (fabric, fit, care). They come before the shop-wide ones.

page.label: Product page layout
page.help: The breadcrumb (Home / category / product) above the page on a computer (the phone never shows it); whether each colour has its own address (/p/product/colour) that opens the page on that colour; and where a colour's address points search engines: the main product (one strong page) or the colour page itself, for the whole shop and per category.

gallery.label: Product photos
gallery.help: The ‹ › buttons over the main photo, the thumbnail strip (on a computer down the side or under the photo), the full-screen photo on a tap, double tap or pinch, which drawing views show while a colour has no photo yet, and the tag or discount badge on the first photo. The full-screen viewer zooms up to your largest zoom on a phone, and in your click steps on a computer. On a computer the main photo is a little shorter than 4:5 (your px, 0 = the full photo) so the whole picture fits the first screen, and at most your number of thumbnails show beside it, the last one saying "+N".

colour.label: Colours on the product page
colour.help: From how many colours "All N colours" moves up to the "Colour – Navy" line (fewer: right after the last swatch), whether "All N colours" and its sheet with every colour's photo show, the colour's own note under the swatches, and "See true-colour photo" when the colour has one.

size.label: Sizes on the product page
size.help: The measurement line under the sizes, the inches / cm switch on the page (cm is always inside the size chart), the "Runs small · True to size · Runs large" bar, and whether a size sold out in every colour is shown crossed out or left out. "Tell me when it is back" on a crossed-out size and on a product that is off sale: the shopper leaves a mobile number and it joins the back-in-stock list (off until the back-in-stock message is sent).

chart.label: Size chart popup
chart.help: The "Size chart" button and its popup (only on products that have a chart), the unit it opens in, "How to measure" under the table, and the "Ask on WhatsApp" card (needs the shop's WhatsApp number).

stock.label: Stock line
stock.help: The stock line above the buttons, from how many pieces "Only N left" shows (0 = never), the same line on the first photo, and your dispatch time for "ships today if you order before …" (empty: not said).

price.label: Price on the product page
price.help: Whether a discounted product shows the struck price, the percentage and the saving after the bar, and the payment line after the bar when the product has no free delivery: on or off, and your own words for it (empty: the payment methods that are switched on).

trust.label: Promise row
trust.help: The row under the buttons: the exchange window, free delivery over your limit and "100% original", in your order. Each shows only while its fact is true (exchange switched on, a free-delivery limit set); "100% original" is off until you switch it on.

rules.label: Delivery · Exchange · Returns
rules.help: The three cells under the buttons, in your order; each takes its words from your live Smart Rules for the product page (exchange and returns fall back to your policy texts). One opens at a time, its full text across the box. "Try it on in front of the rider" under them is off until you switch it on.

details.label: Product details
details.help: Fabric & care, Size & fit and Description, in your order: each closed, open, or open to its first line with "Read more".

buy.label: Buy buttons
buy.help: "Order Now" beside "Add to Bag", the phone's buy bar at the bottom of the screen (the bottom menu hides on this page), the computer's bar that slides in once the buttons have scrolled away, and "Call to order" with your phone number and hours (needs the shop's phone number).

sweep.label: Light sweeps on the product page
sweep.help: The soft light that runs across the free-delivery line, the stock line, "All N colours", the Colour and Size labels and the size boxes, each on its own switch. It never runs for a visitor who has asked for less motion. The one switch for every sweep of the shop ("Light sweeps across the shop") stops these too.

qa.label: Questions & answers on the product page
qa.help: The questions your team has answered and approved for a product, under its page: the latest one open with its answer, the rest folded, a few at first and "See all questions" for the rest. Under them, "Not answered here?" with the WhatsApp button, while the shop has a WhatsApp number. A product with no answered question shows only the WhatsApp ask, or nothing without a number. No question is ever made up.

celebrate.label: Celebration on the thank-you page
celebrate.help: For an occasion: balloons rising (or light streaking up) with your words in the middle, over the thank-you page right after an order. Off. It never blocks anything — the page works behind it, any tap skips it at once, it runs at most 2.5 seconds, once per customer for each occasion's name (or once per order), only between the first and last day you set. It does not run on a slow connection, a low-end phone or with data saving on; for a customer who asked for less motion it shows only the words, without moving. Add ?celebrate=preview to a thank-you page to see it before switching it on.

sweep.label: Light sweeps across the shop
sweep.help: The slow light that crosses the green buttons, the logo, the announcement strip, the footer's payment row, the bag, the checkout and the account's offer banner, each on its own switch, plus one switch that stops every sweep at once (the product page's own words and size boxes too). All on as designed, except the Add to Bag sweep. The checkout and Order Now buttons keep their sweep when "all other green buttons" is off. A customer who asked for less motion never sees any sweep.
